title: Many common systems can only be understood by explicit simulation

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Many common systems can only be understood by explicit simulation

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Computer simulation is not merely a convenient substitute for mathematical formulas: there are many common systems whose behavior can be determined only by something like explicit simulation, and there can be no easy theory for almost any behavior that seems complex.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: there are many common systems whose behavior cannot in the end be determined at all except by something like an explicit simulation.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Computational Irreducibility” (from p. 737), p. 742. Scope: common natural and artificial systems with complex behavior

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing software and proofs can resolve the assertion for selected formal systems. The broad prevalence and natural-system components remain underdetermined because predictor searches do not prove impossibility and the key terms lack thresholds.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For declared natural and artificial model families, compare explicit evolution with every known analytic or accelerated predictor under a formal runtime criterion. Any general shortcut refutes necessity for that family, whereas lower-bound proofs can confirm it for specific systems.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Failure to find a shortcut is not proof that none exists.

Natural systems also require model-validation data.

"Many common systems" and "easy theory" are not quantified.

fields.value:

data existence: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cook's proof that rule 110 is universal, together with the emulation argument, settles the claim for that constructed system. The sentence also covers many common systems and almost any behavior that seems complex. One universality proof leaves that wider scope open, and a picture that resembles a cellular automaton is not a test of a natural system.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For a universal system such as rule 110, check a published emulation proof that any uniform predictor can itself be emulated, so nothing systematically outruns the system. Listing common natural systems and asking whether each has a closed form is a separate test, and only the first is available now.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Universality blocks a uniform shortcut for every input, while a single input may still have a shortcut.

Looking like a simple program is weak evidence that a natural system is universal.

Common and seems complex are observer-relative.
